text: What is the main purpose of using a 'multi-stage build' in a Dockerfile, as shown for the my-biosim image?
choices: To produce a smaller final runtime image by discarding build-only tools and dependencies used to compile or install packages
To allow the container to run without needing a base operating system image
To automatically push the resulting image to a container registry
To grant root permissions inside the container automatically
explanation: A multi-stage build uses an initial 'builder' stage with full compilers/build tools to install dependencies, then copies only the needed artifacts into a slim final stage, shrinking the final image. Every container still runs on top of a base OS image, so that is not the purpose; pushing to a registry is a separate explicit `docker push` step; and multi-stage builds have no special relationship to root permissions.
